tasks.title: Daemon-side cross-process refresh lock (prereq for live SWEEPER_REPOS)
tasks.notes: The CLI takes a per-repo O_EXCL single-flight lockfile (CLI-vs-CLI only). Before flipping the sweeper on against live SWEEPER_REPOS, the daemon must honor the SAME per-repo lock across a job's whole lifecycle. Its current per-job lock is in-process and cannot see the CLI's file.

prep.what: Make the sweeper daemon honor the same per-repo O_EXCL file lock the CLI uses — so simultaneous CLI and daemon runs on the same repo can't race and corrupt it.
prep.understand: The CLI uses a per-repo O_EXCL lockfile (single-flight). The daemon's per-job lock is in-process — it's invisible to the CLI. If a manual `refresh` call runs while the daemon is mid-prep on the same repo, they race. The fix: the daemon acquires the same file before prep starts and releases it on job completion/failure/timeout. If the lock is busy, the job defers (re-enqueue) rather than crashing.
approach: Find the CLI's lock file path convention (look for O_EXCL, `flock`, or `wx` flag usage in `lib/refresh/`) and the exact file path formula.
In the daemon's job lifecycle, wrap the prep step: try-acquire the per-repo file lock using `fs.openSync(path, 'wx')` → on EEXIST, re-enqueue the job for a later slot → release in `finally`.
Write a test: start a mock CLI holding the lock → start a daemon job on the same repo → assert the daemon defers; release the lock → assert the daemon proceeds.
Add a comment in both the CLI and daemon files cross-referencing the convention so it doesn't drift.
resources: `lib/refresh/` — look for O_EXCL, flock, or `fs.openSync` with `wx` flag for the CLI lock
Daemon job lifecycle code — wherever jobs are claimed and executed
`STATE.md` or the sweeper architecture notes for the lock path convention
Node.js `fs.openSync` + `EEXIST` error code for the O_EXCL pattern

tasks.title: Durable job queue (lease/heartbeat/reclaim, window-aware, priority, cap)
tasks.notes: No blockers. Foundation for the sweeper live run — t21 (Sweeper) and t22 (CI) both depend on this.

prep.what: Build the persistent job queue that backs the sweeper: DB-backed leases, heartbeat, stale-job reclaim, work-window awareness, priority ordering, and a per-repo max-parallel cap.
prep.understand: Right now jobs are ephemeral. You need a `sweeper_jobs` table in the existing PG `todos_platform` DB with: atomic claim (lease), heartbeat to keep the lease alive, stale-lease reclaim (cron: reset expired running jobs), window-aware scheduling (don't mint new jobs outside work hours), priority (high > medium > low), and a per-repo cap. This is the foundation t21 (Sweeper) and t22 (CI lane) depend on — build it clean.
approach: Add the migration: `sweeper_jobs(id, repo_slug, task_type, status, priority, payload jsonb, lease_expires_at, heartbeat_at, worker_id, attempts, max_attempts, created_at, updated_at)` — use PG `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` for atomic claim.
Implement core functions: `claimJob()` (atomic claim + set lease), `heartbeatJob(id)` (bump `lease_expires_at`), `reclaimStale()` (reset jobs where `lease_expires_at < now AND status = 'running'`).
Add window awareness: `shouldMintJobs(windowConfig)` checks `work_window.start`/`end` against current local time before the scheduler enqueues sweep jobs.
Build a `runQueue({ workers: 2, maxPerRepo: 1 })` loop that: runs `reclaimStale()` each cycle, claims up to `workers` jobs respecting per-repo cap and priority, runs each in a tracked async slot.
resources: PG `todos_platform` DB — reuse the `db/migrate.ts` migrations pattern
`lib/pg-board-repository.ts` — follow its PG client pattern for the new repository
PostgreSQL `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` docs — the standard atomic queue claim pattern
`config.json` `work_window` shape — reuse for the window-aware gate
